hero.short_description: Sermorelin is the synthetic 29-amino-acid fragment of human growth hormone-releasing hormone, GHRH(1-29), ending in a C-terminal amide. Researchers use it as a reference GHRH-receptor ligand in growth-hormone-axis studies. Veracue supplies it as a Research Use Only material for laboratory work. Published literature describes the molecule, not this material, so it does not establish purity, treatment effect or safety for any research lot.

body: Sermorelin is a synthetic peptide consisting of the first 29 amino acids of human growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH), with a C-terminal amide. Native GHRH has 44 residues. The 1–29 fragment has been described as the shortest synthetic peptide with the full biological activity of GHRH (Prakash & Goa, 1999), which made it a standard reference sequence.

In laboratory research, Sermorelin is studied as an agonist ligand for the GHRH receptor on anterior pituitary somatotroph cells, within growth-hormone-axis research. It is not growth hormone (HGH), which is a much larger protein. Research findings describe defined experimental systems and do not imply any human use.

subsections.body: Sermorelin is a single linear chain without cysteine or disulfide bonds. Its sequence carries three arginines, two lysines and a free N-terminal amine, plus one methionine at position 27. Sermorelin acetate is the acetate salt of this same peptide: the sequence is identical, but the salt adds counterion mass. For that reason, the form on a lot's documentation determines which formula weight applies.

The GHRH receptor is a G protein-coupled receptor on pituitary somatotrophs, related to the receptors for VIP and secretin. It signals mainly through adenylyl cyclase and cyclic AMP. By contrast, the ghrelin (GHS) receptor couples to phospholipase C and calcium. Sermorelin therefore belongs on the GHRH side of growth-hormone-axis research.

Native GHRH is cleaved at its N-terminus in plasma to an inactive fragment, so the unmodified 1–29 sequence is enzymatically labile. Its methionine can oxidize, and its basic residues bind counterions. Each of these features can change what is actually in a vial, which is why identity, purity and peptide content are verified lot by lot.

body: Reverse-phase HPLC reports chromatographic purity: the share of detected material eluting as the main peak. However, it does not confirm identity, and a closely related peptide can give an equally clean trace. It also reflects only what the detector sees at the chosen wavelength.

Mass spectrometry, usually ESI-MS or MALDI-TOF, checks whether the measured mass matches Sermorelin's theoretical value. Yet an intact mass cannot prove sequence order, so tandem MS or another orthogonal method adds confidence where it matters. ESI spectra usually show several multiply charged ions, so reported masses are typically deconvoluted values. Mass data can also flag modified species; methionine oxidation is one example.

Finally, net peptide content, from amino acid or elemental analysis, shows how much of the powder is peptide rather than counterions and water. It is a separate figure from HPLC purity, and both matter.
analytical_characterization.veracue_scope_note: Veracue's site describes a general approach that pairs RP-HPLC purity with mass spectrometry identity, using third-party laboratories named in its COA archive. That is a site-wide practice, not a Sermorelin result.

body: A certificate of analysis describes one lot, never the compound in general. So the first check is simple: the lot number on the COA should match the vial and the order record.

A complete Sermorelin COA separates product identity, lot number, chemical form, HPLC result with chromatogram, MS result with observed and theoretical mass, test date and testing laboratory. Net peptide content adds value when concentration accuracy matters. Together, they make results traceable.
Veracue's public COA archive lists lot numbers, laboratories and test dates for documented compounds; a Sermorelin lot is not yet listed. Lot documentation can be requested through the contact page.

comparison.body: Sermorelin, Tesamorelin and CJC-1295 act at the GHRH receptor; Ipamorelin acts at the ghrelin receptor. They are distinct molecules and not interchangeable. The table compares documented structure and receptor context only, with no ranking.

search_intent.h2: Sermorelin Peptide Benefits: Research Interest, Not Outcomes
search_intent.body: Searches for Sermorelin benefits usually ask what the peptide does. The well-documented property is narrow: Sermorelin stimulates growth hormone release from the anterior pituitary via the GHRH receptor. Research interest therefore centers on receptor pharmacology, somatotroph signaling and analog design. A measurable change in a cell or animal model is not an established clinical outcome, and this page makes no health, body-composition or anti-aging claims.

search_intent.h2: Sermorelin Side Effects: Outside the Scope of This Page
search_intent.body: Human safety information is outside the scope of a Research Use Only product page. Published observations exist, but each belongs to its own study design, population, formulation and exposure conditions. Reading them outside that context can mislead. This page therefore does not summarize adverse events, offer medical advice or provide human-use guidance. Clinical questions belong with a licensed healthcare professional.

Veracue does not provide human dosing, administration, reconstitution or scheduling information for Sermorelin, and this page contains none. In laboratory settings, experimental conditions come from a researcher's own validated study design, informed by the primary literature for the model in use and by the documented identity and peptide content of the actual lot. A supplier's product page cannot replace that validation work.

search_intent.h2: Does Sermorelin Work? How Results Are Interpreted
search_intent.body: Research results depend on the experimental model, the biological endpoint, exposure conditions, assay method and species. Peptide stability in the test system matters too. A GH-release readout in cultured pituitary cells answers a different question from a receptor-binding assay, and neither predicts outcomes in people. Accordingly, before-and-after claims found online are not research results, and this page presents none.

J_problem_research_solution_sections.title: Similar names, different molecules
J_problem_research_solution_sections.research_problem: Sermorelin appears as sermorelin, GRF(1-29)NH2 and hGHRH(1-29)-NH2. Meanwhile, Mod GRF 1-29 and CJC-1295 share its backbone but are different compounds.
J_problem_research_solution_sections.practical_approach: Anchor identity to the sequence, not the name. Sermorelin is the unmodified 1–29 amide, YADAIFTNSYRKVLGQLSARKLLQDIMSR-NH2. Any substitution, D-amino acid or added group makes it a different molecule, even when the product name looks similar. A label or COA should therefore state the exact sequence or an unambiguous name, and it should match across listing, vial and certificate.

J_problem_research_solution_sections.title: High purity does not prove identity
J_problem_research_solution_sections.research_problem: A single sharp HPLC peak is reassuring, but it only shows that most detected material elutes together. A related peptide could produce the same clean trace.
J_problem_research_solution_sections.practical_approach: Treat purity and identity as separate questions. An HPLC result should be paired with a mass spectrometry result from the same lot, reported as observed against theoretical mass. Documentation that offers only one of the two is incomplete, however high the purity figure.

J_problem_research_solution_sections.title: What mass data can and cannot show
J_problem_research_solution_sections.research_problem: Intact mass confirms that a sample fits the expected formula. Still, a rearranged sequence with the same composition would give the same mass.
J_problem_research_solution_sections.practical_approach: For routine procurement, intact mass plus HPLC is the usual baseline. Where sequence certainty matters, tandem MS or another orthogonal method adds evidence. Mass data also help flag minor modified species; because Sermorelin contains methionine, oxidation is one example that characterization can detect.

J_problem_research_solution_sections.title: Weighed powder is not all peptide
J_problem_research_solution_sections.research_problem: With five basic residues and a free N-terminus, Sermorelin binds counterions. Lyophilized peptide powders also retain some water, so gross weight overstates the peptide present.
J_problem_research_solution_sections.practical_approach: Net peptide content, measured by amino acid analysis or nitrogen elemental analysis, quantifies the peptide fraction. It is a separate figure from HPLC purity. When concentration accuracy matters, researchers look for it on the COA or request it from the supplier. Without it, two lots with identical purity can still differ in actual peptide amount.

J_problem_research_solution_sections.title: Free base or salt: the form must be stated
J_problem_research_solution_sections.research_problem: Sermorelin and Sermorelin acetate share one sequence but not one formula weight. If the form is unstated, mass-based calculations can carry a silent error.
J_problem_research_solution_sections.practical_approach: Confirm the chemical form on the lot's COA and use the matching formula weight. Treat the free-base values on this page as reference values only. Where documentation does not state the form, record it as unknown rather than assuming one.

J_problem_research_solution_sections.title: Generic certificates versus lot-specific COAs
J_problem_research_solution_sections.research_problem: Some documents are specification sheets or certificates reused across batches. Neither describes the vial actually on the bench.
J_problem_research_solution_sections.practical_approach: A useful COA names a lot that matches the vial, gives a test date and a named laboratory, and reports measured results rather than target specifications. Keeping it with the relevant notebook entry links each result to its starting material. If questions arise later, the certificate and the data can be compared directly, lot against lot.

J_problem_research_solution_sections.title: The native sequence is enzymatically labile
J_problem_research_solution_sections.research_problem: Native GHRH is cleaved at its N-terminus in plasma, leaving an inactive fragment. Unrecognized degradation can look like a weak or inconsistent response.
J_problem_research_solution_sections.practical_approach: Researchers therefore treat stability in their chosen system as an experimental variable rather than an assumption, and they document preparation and handling conditions consistently across experiments. That awareness also explains why later GHRH analogs, such as CJC-1295, were designed for greater enzymatic resistance, and why they cannot stand in for Sermorelin.

J_problem_research_solution_sections.title: Choosing a comparator for the right pathway
J_problem_research_solution_sections.research_problem: Sermorelin and Ipamorelin are often discussed together, yet they act at different receptors with different signaling. Mixing them up blurs what an experiment is actually testing.
J_problem_research_solution_sections.practical_approach: Matching comparators to the question keeps interpretation clean: GHRH-receptor ligands for GHRH-pathway questions, GHS-receptor ligands for ghrelin-pathway questions. Naming each molecule precisely in methods sections, including any substitutions or modifications, also makes the work reproducible and easier to compare with published studies.

J_problem_research_solution_sections.title: Literature is not a product claim
J_problem_research_solution_sections.research_problem: Much published Sermorelin work involved a licensed drug product in clinical settings. It is easy to read those findings as statements about a research chemical.
J_problem_research_solution_sections.practical_approach: Keep three things apart: what a study showed, in which model and formulation, and what a specific lot has been shown to be. Literature can inform hypotheses, endpoints and assay design. It cannot establish the identity, purity or suitability of any commercial research material.

J_problem_research_solution_sections.title: A procurement record that holds up later
J_problem_research_solution_sections.research_problem: Months later, a result may need to be traced to its starting material. Without organized records, that is rarely possible.
J_problem_research_solution_sections.practical_approach: For each lot, a defensible record keeps the listing snapshot, lot-specific COA, stated chemical form, net peptide content if available, receipt date, labeled storage conditions and the experiments that used it. Consistent records make lot-to-lot differences visible and allow unexpected results to be traced back quickly rather than reconstructed from memory.

L_aeo_direct_answers.a: Sermorelin peptide is a synthetic 29-amino-acid fragment of human growth hormone-releasing hormone, GHRH(1-29), with a C-terminal amide. Its free-base formula is C149H246N44O42S, about 3357.9 g/mol. Researchers use it as a reference agonist for the GHRH receptor in growth-hormone-axis studies. Veracue supplies it for Research Use Only.

Sermorelin acetate is the acetate salt of the same 29-residue peptide. The sequence is identical, but acetate counterions add mass, so its formula weight differs from the free-base value. Researchers should use the formula weight matching the chemical form stated on the lot's certificate of analysis.

L_aeo_direct_answers.q: What is Sermorelin used for in research?
L_aeo_direct_answers.a: Sermorelin is used in laboratory research as a defined ligand for the GHRH receptor on anterior pituitary somatotroph cells. It supports receptor-signaling studies, serves as the parent sequence when comparing GHRH analogs, and is a model for peptide-stability work. These are research applications, not human uses.

Sermorelin is characterized mainly by reverse-phase HPLC, which reports chromatographic purity, and mass spectrometry, which checks the measured mass against the theoretical value. Tandem MS adds sequence evidence. Amino acid or elemental analysis measures net peptide content, which accounts for counterions and water in the powder.

L_aeo_direct_answers.q: How is Sermorelin different from Ipamorelin?
L_aeo_direct_answers.a: Sermorelin is a 29-residue GHRH fragment acting at the GHRH receptor, which signals mainly through cAMP. Ipamorelin is an unrelated synthetic pentapeptide acting at the ghrelin (GHS) receptor, which couples to phospholipase C and calcium. They are separate research tools, not variants of one another.

L_aeo_direct_answers.q: How is Sermorelin different from Tesamorelin?
L_aeo_direct_answers.a: Sermorelin is the unmodified 1–29 fragment of human GHRH. Tesamorelin uses the full 44-amino-acid GHRH sequence with a trans-3-hexenoyl group on its N-terminal tyrosine. Both act at the GHRH receptor, but they differ in length, mass and N-terminal chemistry, so they are distinct research materials.

L_aeo_direct_answers.q: What should a researcher look for in a Sermorelin COA?
L_aeo_direct_answers.a: A Sermorelin COA should state product identity, chemical form, a lot number matching the vial, test date and testing laboratory. It should report an HPLC result with chromatogram and a mass spectrometry result with observed and theoretical mass. Net peptide content is a useful addition.
